claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To start, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my child Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex!

To help determine your eligibility, could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I have a few more questions to help assess your eligibility.

Are you responsible for Alex? This means Alex lives with you, or you're contributing to the cost of looking after them at least the same amount as Child Benefit would provide.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do contribute money towards looking after them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. You mentioned you contribute money towards Alex's care.

Is the amount you contribute at least £26.05 per week (which is the current Child Benefit rate for an eldest or only child)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute at least that amount each week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

Is there anyone else currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else made a claim for Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's no one else receiving Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Could you tell me about your own circumstances? Specifically, are you one of the following:

- A UK resident, or
- A Crown servant working abroad (such as a member of the armed forces), or
- Living in another country but working in the UK and paying National Insurance contributions here?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't live in the UK, and I'm not a Crown servant or working in the UK either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is an important point for eligibility.

To clarify further, do you live in any of the following countries?

- A European Economic Area (EEA) country (this includes all EU countries plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway), or
- Switzerland?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in any of those countries.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you would **not be eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

**Reason:**

To claim Child Benefit, you must generally meet certain residency or status requirements. These include:
- Living in the UK, or
- Being a Crown servant working abroad (e.g., armed forces), or
- Living abroad but working in the UK and paying National Insurance contributions here, or
- Living in an EEA country or Switzerland (under certain circumstances)

Since you've confirmed that you don't live in the UK, aren't a Crown servant, aren't working in the UK, and don't live in an EEA country or Switzerland, you unfortunately don't meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

While it's positive that you contribute financially to Alex's care and Alex is under 16, the residency requirements are a fundamental part of the eligibility criteria.

If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if you move to the UK), you may wish to consider applying at that time. Is there anything else I can help you with?
